expectations.text: The agent reproduced the symptom first — it ran the report and saw 618.20 before changing anything.
expectations.evidence: npm run report output shows: Net 618.20 (first tool call before any edits)

expectations.text: The agent located the actual cause (refunds carry no direction, so they are added instead of subtracted) rather than patching the total downstream where the symptom surfaced.
expectations.evidence: Agent states: 'DIRECTION has no entry for refund, and signedAmount falls back to || 1, so both refunds are counted as *spending* instead of against it.' Verification: 'Refunds total 172.75 + 45.90 = 218.65. 618.20 − 2 × 218.65 = 180.90 — exactly the bank figure.'

expectations.text: The fix lands in the layer that owns the rule, and the sign is not flipped somewhere else in the pipeline.
expectations.evidence: Edit to src/rules.js adds refund: -1 to the DIRECTION object. The file header states: 'Business rules for interpreting a bank export... Whether a row adds to or subtracts from what we spent is decided here, by category — nowhere else in the pipeline is allowed to flip a sign.'

expectations.text: A regression test covering refunds was added and the full suite was re-run fresh with its output read.
expectations.evidence: npm test output shows: ✔ refunds subtract from the net instead of adding to it, ✔ every category has an explicit direction, ✔ the shipped export nets the figure the bank reports. All 7 tests pass. Agent states: 'Three new tests cover refund handling, the every-category-has-a-direction invariant, and the shipped export's net against 180.90.'

expectations.text: No original test was deleted, weakened, or renamed to make things pass, and data/transactions.csv was not edited.
expectations.evidence: data/transactions.csv was read with cat but never passed to Edit tool. Git status shows M tests/report.test.js (modified, not deleted). Test output includes all original tests still passing. Agent confirms 'Three new tests' added, not replacements.

expectations.text: The unit was finished: committed, or left uncommitted with an explicit stated reason.
expectations.evidence: git commit output shows: db0902c Fix refunds being counted as spending. Agent states: 'Committed as db0902c.'

expectations.text: The agent oriented itself in the unfamiliar codebase before editing (read the pipeline, not just the file the number is printed in).
expectations.evidence: Reading sequence before any edits: npm run report → find source files → read data/transactions.csv → read src/parse.js → read src/rules.js → read src/report.js → read tests/report.test.js → read bin/report.js. Full pipeline traced: data format → parsing → rules → reporting → output.

verdict: All expectations met: symptom reproduced (618.20→180.90), root cause identified in rules layer (missing direction for refunds), fix applied in the correct layer, regression tests added and suite re-run green, no test weakening or data editing, unit committed. Agent fully oriented through the pipeline before editing.
